keywordsHtml:
1. Severe chronic plaque psoriasis – Indicates disease severity, signaling the need for systemic/biologic therapy rather than topical or supportive treatments.
  2. Refractory to methotrexate and phototherapy – Shows treatment failure, pointing specifically to next-line biologic therapy.

A.title: TNF-α inhibitors
A.body:
TNF-α inhibitors (e.g., etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab) are biologic agents used in moderate-to-severe psoriasis refractory to conventional systemic therapies like methotrexate or phototherapy.
They target tumor necrosis factor-alpha, a key cytokine in psoriasis pathogenesis, reducing inflammation and keratinocyte proliferation.
Chosen when first-line systemic therapies fail, they can achieve rapid and sustained clearance of psoriatic plaques.
A.bodyHtml:
• TNF-α inhibitors (e.g., etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab) are biologic agents used in moderate-to-severe psoriasis refractory to conventional systemic therapies like methotrexate or phototherapy.
  • They target tumor necrosis factor-alpha, a key cytokine in psoriasis pathogenesis, reducing inflammation and keratinocyte proliferation.
  • Chosen when first-line systemic therapies fail, they can achieve rapid and sustained clearance of psoriatic plaques.
A.systemInvolved: Immune system / Dermatology (Psoriasis – autoimmune skin disease),

B.title: Topical corticosteroids
B.body:
Useful for mild or limited psoriasis, primarily applied to localized plaques.
Not sufficient for severe, refractory disease.
B.bodyHtml:
• Useful for mild or limited psoriasis, primarily applied to localized plaques.
  • Not sufficient for severe, refractory disease.

C.title: Retinoids only
C.body:
Systemic retinoids (e.g., acitretin) can be used in psoriasis but are less effective alone for severe refractory disease.
Often combined with phototherapy or other systemic agents.
C.bodyHtml:
• Systemic retinoids (e.g., acitretin) can be used in psoriasis but are less effective alone for severe refractory disease.
  • Often combined with phototherapy or other systemic agents.

D.title: Emollients
D.body:
Provide symptomatic relief by moisturizing skin and reducing scaling.
They do not modify disease progression or treat severe psoriasis.
D.bodyHtml:
• Provide symptomatic relief by moisturizing skin and reducing scaling.
  • They do not modify disease progression or treat severe psoriasis.

E.title: Antibiotics
E.body:
Not indicated unless there is secondary bacterial infection.
Psoriasis is an autoimmune inflammatory disease, not infectious.
E.bodyHtml:
• Not indicated unless there is secondary bacterial infection.
  • Psoriasis is an autoimmune inflammatory disease, not infectious.

keyConcept: In severe chronic plaque psoriasis refractory to conventional systemic therapy, biologic agents such as TNF-α inhibitors are the treatment of choice, targeting immune-mediated inflammation. Topical or supportive therapies are insufficient for systemic disease control.

diagram.name: Severe Chronic Plaque Psoriasis – Biologic Therapy (Treatment Escalation Pathway)
diagram.caption: The diagram illustrates the stepwise escalation of therapy in severe chronic plaque psoriasis after failure of methotrexate and UVB phototherapy, highlighting the role of biologic agents. It shows how targeted biologics—TNF-α inhibitors, IL-12/23 inhibitors, and IL-17 inhibitors—act on the immune system to suppress pathogenic cytokines, reduce inflammation, and improve skin clearance in refractory disease.
